intro: Welcome back! In class you sometimes miss a word or don't know what it means, and that's normal. Today you learn short questions that help, like Can you repeat that, please? and How do you spell …?, plus the instructions teachers use, like Listen, Repeat and Open your book. Warm-up: how do you ask someone to say something again?
teachingNotes: Teach the questions as fixed chunks: 'Can you repeat that, please?', 'Can you speak more slowly, please?', 'What does … mean?', 'How do you spell …?', 'What's … in English?'. Don't explain do-support, modal verbs or the simple present; the learner hasn't met them yet.
Common error: 'How to spell your name?' (a direct translation of 'Bagaimana mengeja…'). The right question is 'How do you spell your name?'. Similar: 'What mean busy?' → 'What does busy mean?'.
Say 'speak more slowly' (not 'more slow'). A short 'Sorry?' or 'Pardon?' with the voice going up also means 'please say it again'. 'Repeat!' alone sounds like an order: always add please.

Classroom instructions are short and start with the action word, with no 'you': Listen. Repeat. Open your book. Teach opposites together (open/close, stand up/sit down). 'Repeat after me' means say it again after the teacher.
Spelling answers use the letter names from the alphabet lesson (G = 'jee', J = 'jay', E = 'ee', I = 'eye'). Numbers come in a later lesson, so avoid instructions like 'Turn to page 25'.

If the learner asks why 'do' / 'does' is in the question: say it's a small helper word English questions need, with no meaning of its own here (it is not 'melakukan'), which is why a word-by-word translation fails. Use 'does' in What does … mean? and 'do' in How do you spell …?; learn both questions whole, the rule comes later.
'Sorry?' with the voice going up is a question meaning 'apa tadi?', not an apology. Learners met sorry as 'maaf, after a mistake' in the greetings lesson, so point out the difference.

slow vs slowly in plain words: slow describes a person or thing (a slow bus = bis yang lambat), slowly describes how someone does something (speak slowly = bicara dengan pelan). Don't use the word 'adverb'.
Short forms the learner meets here: What's = What is, don't = do not, you're = you are. 'your' means both -mu (one person) and kalian (a group): Open your book / Open your books.

keyPoints.title: Asking someone to repeat or slow down
keyPoints.explanation: Can you repeat that, please? or Can you say that again, please? asks someone to say it again. Can you speak more slowly, please? asks them to slow down. A short Sorry? or Pardon? (voice going up) works too.

examples.en: Sorry? Can you repeat that, please?
Can you speak more slowly, please?

id.title: Minta diulang atau bicara lebih pelan
id.explanation: Can you repeat that, please? atau Can you say that again, please? untuk minta seseorang mengulang. Can you speak more slowly, please? untuk minta mereka bicara lebih pelan. Sorry? atau Pardon? yang singkat (dengan nada naik) juga bisa.

keyPoints.title: Asking about a word
keyPoints.explanation: Meaning: What does + word + mean? Spelling: How do you spell + word? The English word: What's + word + in English? Never 'How to spell…?'.

id.title: Bertanya tentang sebuah kata
id.explanation: Arti: What does + kata + mean? Ejaan: How do you spell + kata? Bahasa Inggrisnya: What's + kata + in English? Jangan pakai 'How to spell…?'.

keyPoints.title: Classroom instructions
keyPoints.explanation: Instructions start with the action word: Listen. Repeat. Read. Write. Open your book. Close your book. Look at the board. Stand up. Sit down. Work in pairs.

id.title: Instruksi di kelas
id.explanation: Instruksi diawali kata kerja (kata yang menunjukkan tindakan): Listen. Repeat. Read. Write. Open your book. Close your book. Look at the board. Stand up. Sit down. Work in pairs.

assessment.prompt: You didn't hear what the teacher said. Write a polite question to ask her to say it again.
acceptableAnswers: can you say that again please
could you say that again please
can you say it again please
sorry can you repeat that please
sorry could you repeat that please
excuse me can you repeat that please
assessment.rubric: Correct: Can/Could you repeat that, please? or Can you say that again, please? Without please = 90. 'Repeat!' or 'Repeat please' = 50 (sounds like an order). 'You repeat?' = 30.

assessment.prompt: Rina says your name, but she speaks very quietly. Write ONE short polite word you can say, with your voice going up, so she says it again.
assessment.rubric: Correct: Sorry? or Pardon? 'What?' = 40 (understood, but can sound rude). 'Excuse me?' = 80.

assessment.prompt: You see the word 'tired' in your book. Write a question to ask your teacher what it means.
acceptableAnswers: what does the word tired mean
excuse me what does tired mean
what is the meaning of tired
what does tired mean in indonesian
assessment.rubric: Correct: What does 'tired' mean? 'What is tired mean?' or 'What mean tired?' = 40 (meaning clear, form wrong).

assessment.prompt: Your new classmate says, 'My name is Wahyu.' Write a question to ask him for the letters of his name.
acceptableAnswers: how do you spell your name
how do you spell your name please
how do you spell it please
can you spell your name please
could you spell your name please
sorry how do you spell your name
assessment.rubric: Correct: How do you spell your name / Wahyu / it? Accept Can you spell it, please? 'How to spell your name?' = 40 (common error: missing 'do you').

The teacher says 'Stand up.' Later she wants everyone back on their chairs. Write her instruction (two words).

blocks.text: Missing words is normal, so ask! **Can you repeat that, please?** or **Can you say that again, please?** asks someone to say it again. If someone talks too fast: **Can you speak more slowly, please?** For a quick question, just say **Sorry?** or **Pardon?** with your voice going up.

id.text: Ketinggalan kata itu biasa, jadi bertanyalah! **Can you repeat that, please?** atau **Can you say that again, please?** meminta orang mengulang. Kalau orang bicara terlalu cepat: **Can you speak more slowly, please?** Untuk pertanyaan singkat, cukup bilang **Sorry?** atau **Pardon?** dengan nada naik.

rows.en: Sorry? Can you repeat that, please?
rows.note: Sorry? with the voice going up = what did you say?

id.note: Sorry? dengan nada naik = tadi bilang apa?

rows.en: Can you speak more slowly, please?

blocks.text: Say **slowly**, not 'slow': *slow* describes a person or thing (*a slow bus*), and *slowly* describes **how** someone does something (*speak slowly*). And always add **please**: 'Repeat!' alone sounds like an order. *Can you … , please?* is not really asking if the person is able to: it's the polite way to ask someone to do something, like *bisa … ?* or *tolong …*.

id.text: Ucapkan **slowly**, bukan 'slow': *slow* menjelaskan orang atau benda (*a slow bus* = bis yang lambat), sedangkan *slowly* menjelaskan **cara** orang melakukan sesuatu (*speak slowly* = bicara dengan pelan). Dan selalu tambahkan **please**: 'Repeat!' saja terdengar seperti perintah. *Can you … , please?* sebenarnya tidak menanyakan apakah orangnya mampu: ini cara sopan meminta orang melakukan sesuatu, seperti *bisa … ?* atau *tolong …*.

blocks.text: **Wait, isn't *sorry* for mistakes?** Yes, but **Sorry?** said like a question, with your voice going **up** at the end, means *apa tadi?* (please say it again). It's not an apology here. **Pardon?** means the same and is a bit more formal. And in *I don't understand*, **don't** is the short form of **do not** (*tidak*).

id.text: **Lho, bukannya *sorry* untuk minta maaf?** Betul, tapi **Sorry?** yang diucapkan seperti pertanyaan, dengan nada **naik** di akhir, artinya *apa tadi?* (tolong ulangi). Di sini itu bukan permintaan maaf. **Pardon?** artinya sama dan sedikit lebih formal. Lalu di *I don't understand*, **don't** adalah bentuk pendek dari **do not** (*tidak*).

blocks.prompt: Your friend from London talks very fast. What's the best thing to say?
options: Can you speak more slowly, please?
blocks.explain: It's polite (Can you … , please?) and uses slowly, the right word after speak.

id.explain: Kalimat ini sopan (Can you … , please?) dan memakai slowly, kata yang tepat setelah speak.
id.prompt: Temanmu dari London bicara sangat cepat. Apa yang paling tepat kamu ucapkan?

blocks.text: To ask the meaning: **What does** *busy* **mean?** To ask the letters: **How do you spell** *Bandung*? To ask for the English word: **What's** *meja* **in English?** The answer to a spelling question uses letter names: *B-A-N-D-U-N-G*.

id.text: Untuk menanyakan arti: **What does** *busy* **mean?** Untuk menanyakan hurufnya: **How do you spell** *Bandung*? Untuk menanyakan kata bahasa Inggrisnya: **What's** *meja* **in English?** Jawaban untuk pertanyaan ejaan memakai nama huruf: *B-A-N-D-U-N-G*.

rows.en: How do you say 'terima kasih' in English? — Thank you.
rows.id: Bagaimana bilang 'terima kasih' dalam bahasa Inggris? — Thank you.

blocks.text: Don't say 'How to spell your name?' (a direct translation of *Bagaimana mengeja…*). The question is **How do you spell your name?**. Same with meaning: **What does it mean?**, not 'What mean?'.

id.text: Jangan bilang 'How to spell your name?' (terjemahan langsung dari *Bagaimana mengeja…*). Pertanyaannya adalah **How do you spell your name?**. Sama dengan arti: **What does it mean?**, bukan 'What mean?'.

blocks.text: **Why *do* and *does*?** English questions often need a small helper word. Here *do* / *does* has no meaning of its own (it isn't *melakukan*); it just makes the sentence a question. Indonesian doesn't need it, so a word-by-word translation goes wrong: *Bagaimana mengeja…* → 'How to spell…?', *Apa arti…* → 'What mean…?'. It's **does** in *What does … mean?* and **do** in *How do you spell …?*. The rule for when to use which comes in a later lesson; for now, learn the two questions whole. And **What's** is the short form of **What is**.

id.text: **Kenapa ada *do* dan *does*?** Pertanyaan bahasa Inggris sering butuh kata bantu kecil. Di sini *do* / *does* tidak punya arti sendiri (bukan *melakukan*); kata itu hanya membuat kalimatnya jadi pertanyaan. Bahasa Indonesia tidak memerlukannya, jadi terjemahan kata per kata jadi salah: *Bagaimana mengeja…* → 'How to spell…?', *Apa arti…* → 'What mean…?'. Pakai **does** di *What does … mean?* dan **do** di *How do you spell …?*. Aturan kapan memakai yang mana ada di pelajaran berikutnya; untuk sekarang, hafalkan kedua pertanyaan itu secara utuh. Lalu **What's** adalah bentuk pendek dari **What is**.

blocks.prompt: You read the word 'quiet'. Which question is correct?
blocks.explain: The pattern is What does + word + mean? The word goes in the middle and mean comes last. Does is the small helper word the question needs; without it ('What mean…?') it's a word-by-word translation.

id.explain: Polanya What does + kata + mean? Katanya di tengah dan mean di akhir. Does adalah kata bantu yang dibutuhkan pertanyaan ini; tanpa does ('What mean…?') itu terjemahan kata per kata.
id.prompt: Kamu membaca kata 'quiet'. Pertanyaan mana yang benar?

blocks.text: Teachers give short instructions. They start with the action word and don't say 'you': **Listen.** **Repeat.** **Read.** **Write.** **Look at the board.** **Open your book.** **Sit down.** **Work in pairs.** Adding **please** makes them softer.

id.text: Guru memberi instruksi pendek. Instruksi dimulai dengan kata kerja (kata untuk tindakan, misalnya *listen, write*) dan tanpa 'you': **Listen.** **Repeat.** **Read.** **Write.** **Look at the board.** **Open your book.** **Sit down.** **Work in pairs.** Tambahan **please** membuatnya lebih halus.

blocks.text: Learn instructions in pairs of opposites: **open ↔ close**, **stand up ↔ sit down**. Then one word helps you remember the other. And **your** means both *-mu* (one person) and *kalian* (a group): *Open your book* / *Open your books*. English uses the same word.

id.text: Pelajari instruksi berpasangan dengan lawan katanya: **open ↔ close**, **stand up ↔ sit down**. Jadi satu kata membantumu mengingat yang lain. Lalu **your** bisa berarti *-mu* (satu orang) atau *kalian* (banyak orang): *Open your book* / *Open your books*. Bahasa Inggris memakai kata yang sama.

blocks.prompt: The teacher says: 'Repeat after me: Good morning.' What do you do?
blocks.explain: Repeat after me means say the same words after the teacher.

id.explain: Repeat after me artinya ucapkan kata yang sama setelah guru.
id.prompt: Guru bilang: 'Repeat after me: Good morning.' Apa yang kamu lakukan?

blocks.text: In a Zoom or Google Meet class you hear a few extra instructions: **Turn on your camera, please.** **You're on mute.** And when the sound is bad, you can say: **Sorry, I can't hear you.**

id.text: Di kelas Zoom atau Google Meet kamu mendengar beberapa instruksi tambahan: **Turn on your camera, please.** **You're on mute.** Dan kalau suaranya jelek, kamu bisa bilang: **Sorry, I can't hear you.**

blocks.prompt: Your teacher on Zoom says: 'Sari, you're on mute!' What do you do?
blocks.explain: On mute means your microphone is off, so the teacher can't hear you. Turn it on.

id.explain: On mute artinya mikrofonmu mati, jadi guru tidak bisa mendengarmu. Nyalakan mikrofonnya.
id.prompt: Gurumu di Zoom bilang: 'Sari, you're on mute!' Apa yang kamu lakukan?

id.intro: Selamat datang kembali! Di kelas kadang kamu ketinggalan kata atau tidak tahu artinya, dan itu wajar. Hari ini kamu belajar pertanyaan pendek yang membantu, seperti Can you repeat that, please? dan How do you spell …?, plus instruksi yang dipakai guru, seperti Listen, Repeat dan Open your book. Pemanasan: bagaimana cara meminta seseorang mengulang ucapannya?
suggestedQuestions: Kenapa tidak boleh bilang 'How to spell your name?'
Bagaimana menanyakan bahasa Inggris dari sebuah kata?

assessment.class-1: Kamu tidak mendengar ucapan guru. Tulis pertanyaan sopan dalam bahasa Inggris untuk memintanya mengulang.
assessment.class-2: Rina menyebut namamu, tapi suaranya pelan sekali. Tulis SATU kata sopan dalam bahasa Inggris yang kamu ucapkan dengan nada naik supaya dia mengulanginya.
assessment.class-3: Kamu melihat kata 'tired' di bukumu. Tulis pertanyaan dalam bahasa Inggris untuk menanyakan artinya kepada guru.
assessment.class-4: Teman sekelasmu yang baru berkata, 'My name is Wahyu.' Tulis pertanyaan dalam bahasa Inggris untuk memintanya mengeja namanya.
assessment.class-5: Dengarkan guru. Kamu harus melihat ke mana? Tulis satu atau dua kata dalam bahasa Inggris.
assessment.class-6: Guru berkata 'Stand up.' Lalu dia ingin semua murid duduk kembali. Tulis instruksinya (dua kata dalam bahasa Inggris).
